To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the calcium antimonate technique is a reliable and useful technique for localizing Ca2+ in ovules, (2) calcium antimonate precipitates occur in the ovule in the same sequence as the events of fertilization, (3) calcium antimonates occur in the ovules of emasculated flowers, and (4) calcium antimonation in ovules is correlated with the ability of ovules to be fertilized.
